likely_scanner_gap.observed_output: The four concrete handlers and their complete endpoint signatures were already emitted. Registry discovery therefore succeeded for this sample.
likely_scanner_gap.primary_hypothesis_only: If another scanner misses this shape, inspect support for invoke-interface java.util.Map.put on an erased Map field. This was not the cause of the reported YSP score mismatch.
likely_scanner_gap.secondary_hypothesis_only: Interprocedural substitution from interface parameter p2 to caller concrete allocations remains a generally relevant pattern, but it was successfully resolved here.
likely_scanner_gap.control_flow_hypothesis_only: The QFix early-return/fallthrough shape remains a possible generic edge case, but it did not prevent these four handlers from being emitted.
likely_scanner_gap.not_the_cause: Handler type c is already a DEX interface, not an abstract-class edge case. Adding abstract-class endpoint support alone cannot make this register method a seed.
likely_scanner_gap.recommended_pattern: Recognize invoke-interface Map.put on a receiver loaded from a stable instance field; record key/value parameter expressions at the register method, then resolve literals and concrete handler allocations at callers. Preserve router receiver identity.

two_level_name_semantics.confirmed_difference: YspJSBridge is the native addJavascriptInterface name of the injected f object. The four selector strings are message-handler names looked up inside that same object; they are not alternate Javascript interface registration names.
two_level_name_semantics.identity_requirement: A message handler matches a gold fact only when its selector equals gold.name and its transport binding names YspJSBridge on the same WebView and same injected f object identity.
two_level_name_semantics.report_model: Represent the native injection as transport_bindings(name, WebView identity, registration site, injected object identity), and attach message_handler(selector, endpoint) records to that transport object.
